notes.name: Monero
notes.thesis: Monero is private cash; supply is set by mining and nothing unlocks. Fee activity runs modestly above its year-long pace, and the coin is the cheapest proof-of-work peer per dollar of fees. Positioning and the wider market argue the other way; neither wins over eight weeks.
limitations: DefiLlama has no documented release schedule for XMR

evidence.how: the research leaned lower; the independent reads do not back it: usage points higher; supply is unclear; valuation points neither way — no call

notes.name: Monero
notes.thesis: The balance of evidence tilts lower, but not strongly enough for a directional view: fee demand has not grown against a $10.49B valuation, and crowded longs sit on a falling seven-day trend. Fixed supply caps the downside.
limitations: DefiLlama has no documented release schedule for XMR

evidence.how: the research tilts lower; 1 of 3 items point lower (valuation); supply points higher; usage is unclear — not enough for a call

notes.name: Pump.fun
notes.thesis: PUMP earns far more per dollar of value than its listed peers, but dated team and investor unlocks and a falling price mean the balance of evidence tilts lower, not strongly enough for a directional view.

notes.name: Pump.fun
notes.thesis: Insider unlocks add 4.5% of circulating PUMP over 90 days, the 7-day fee run-rate has slipped below the 30-day, and price sits near its 30-day low. The balance of evidence tilts lower, but not strongly enough for a directional view.

notes.name: Avalanche
notes.thesis: AVAX earns very little against a $4.03B valuation, staking keeps minting, and the token is down 21.5% over 30 days. Institutional mandates are real but mostly undated, so the next eight weeks favour the lower half of the volatility range.

notes.name: Avalanche
notes.thesis: AVAX has real institutional headlines, but its near-term usage economics are weak. Real users are scarce, activity is bot-heavy, and network fees are negligible against FDV while Q3 net issuance was about 2.56M AVAX. Supply and unlock pressure persist.
limitations: facts: DefiLlama: no fees series found

notes.name: ether.fi
notes.thesis: ETHFI trades at 26.4x annualised revenue versus an 11.1x peer median, with new Core Contributor supply starting 6 Nov. Price is weak and the buyback does not shrink float. Positioning is not crowded, which limits squeeze risk but does not fix valuation.
limitations: no "Leads: N of M confirmed." line from the dossier

notes.name: NEAR Protocol
notes.thesis: NEAR trades at 75.5x annualised fees and 220.1x annualised revenue against a 25.5x peer median. Own-chain activity is collapsing, the buyback offsets about a tenth of issuance, and positioning is still long. The Intents business is real but richly priced.
limitations: no "Leads: N of M confirmed." line from the dossier

notes.name: Hyperliquid
notes.thesis: Fees annualise at $1.02B and revenue at $802M, and the 7-day fee pace exceeds the 30-day. But HYPE trades at 111x annualised revenue against a 31x peer median, with 410M future emissions and 238M contributor tokens outstanding.
limitations: the documented schedule covers only 41% of supply — printed as a floor

notes.name: Pepe
notes.thesis: No protocol revenue and no dated catalyst leave PEPE a pure sentiment trade. Price sits at its 30-day and 90-day high, longs are crowded and top wallets are concentrated, so the evidence favours the lower half of the eight-week range.
limitations: too little funding history to judge crowding against the coin's own range — the decision is price location only
facts: DefiLlama: no fees series found

notes.name: Ethereum
notes.thesis: Ethereum's fee base is flat, the recent spike is one-off exploiter flow, supply is inflationary and ETH trades at 1,215× annualised fees against a 217× peer median. Crowded longs and a close at the 30-day low leave the 8-week risk to the downside.

notes.name: Ethereum
notes.thesis: Price sits at the bottom of its 30-day range after a 16.1% monthly fall. ETH trades at 3071.2x annualised revenue versus a 603.0x peer median, and Dencun has compressed L1 fees. The dossier's lean is neutral-to-bear, favouring the lower half.
